# NetPulse

> The VPS inspector built for AI agents: one command from your laptop, health-check your whole fleet, pipe results straight to an agent.

NetPulse is a single-file Python CLI that checks a VPS's network health: egress IP
info (IP, location, ASN, ISP), IP purity (datacenter / residential / proxy traits),
DNS leak detection (resolver geo vs IP geo), streaming & AI unlock tests (Netflix,
Disney+, YouTube Premium, HBO Max, Hulu, Prime Video, TikTok, Spotify, ChatGPT,
Claude, Gemini), IPv6 egress, TCP latency to Cloudflare/Google/Baidu, and download
speed tests.

Key differentiator: agent-friendly fleet inspection. Launch locally with
`--host user@host` (repeatable) — the script is shipped over SSH, executed remotely,
and results return as JSON. Non-interactive, machine-readable, clear exit codes.

## Install

```bash
bash <(curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Genuifx/NetPulse/main/install.sh)
```

Only dependency: `requests` (auto-installed when missing, including on remote hosts).

## Usage

```bash
python3 netpulse.py                                  # check this machine
python3 netpulse.py --host root@1.2.3.4              # launch locally, run remotely
python3 netpulse.py --host root@a --host root@b --json | jq .   # fleet inspection
python3 netpulse.py --share                          # save Markdown report
```

`--host` needs key-based SSH auth (`BatchMode=yes`) and `python3` on the remote host.

## JSON schema (--json)

Single host returns one object; multiple `--host` flags return an array.
Fields: `tool`, `version`, `timestamp`, `host`, `ip`, `purity`, `dns`, `unlock`
(map of service name to HTTP status code), `ipv6`, `latency`, `speed`, `summary`.
On failure: an `error` field and a non-zero exit code.

## Notes

- Unlock tests are HTTP-status triage only (200 ≈ reachable, 403/451 ≈ likely
  geo-blocked); use a dedicated script to confirm services like Netflix.
- For your own servers only. MIT licensed.
